name: bge-small-rrf-v2
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (config.json max_position_embeddings 512). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: bidirectional encoder (BERT), full attention, no causal mask
notes: ADDED 2026-11-01. Fine-tune of BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (33M, 384-dim, 12 layers) using a self-supervised signal: run the existing hybrid vector+keyword pipeline, take the queries where the two disagree (82% of queries), and train MNRL on those disagreements. Same param count as the base, so no capacity change. Recorded because the card prints ColBERTv2, 'BGE-small base (33M)' and 'This model (33M)' as three columns of one BEIR nDCG@10 table on identical datasets: SciFact 0.646 -> 0.695, NFCorpus 0.330 -> 0.395, SciDocs 0.178 -> 0.188, ArguAna 0.419 -> 0.424, FiQA 0.328 -> 0.328 (tie). Read the win as narrow-but-real on NFCorpus and SciFact and noise elsewhere: the headline '+19.5% NDCG' is the relative NFCorpus figure, and three of five datasets move by under 1 point, with FiQA flat and ArguAna -8.4% against ColBERTv2. A sibling repo of the same author (bge-small-rrf-lme-v1) is already in the catalog for LongMemEval; this one is the general-BEIR claim.

benchmarks.name: BEIR NFCorpus NDCG@10
benchmarks.config: Same table: base 0.330 vs this model 0.395 (+0.065, the +19.5% the card advertises). 3.6K docs.

benchmarks.name: BEIR SciDocs NDCG@10
benchmarks.config: Same table: base 0.178 vs this model 0.188 (+0.010). 25K docs. Small in absolute terms.

benchmarks.name: BEIR ArguAna NDCG@10
benchmarks.config: Same table: base 0.419 vs this model 0.424 (+0.005) - a 0.5-point move, i.e. level with the base. Recorded but carries no weight; the card's own 'vs ColBERTv2' column is negative here (-8.4%).

benchmarks.name: BEIR FiQA NDCG@10
benchmarks.config: Same table: base 0.328 vs this model 0.328 - exact tie on 57K docs, so FiQA is not evidence of a gain.
